heading: Step 4: Call the server from the page
body:
A client class sends HTTP requests for the page. Put it in `client/clients`. `HTTPClient` marks the class. `GetRequest("/api/greeting")` makes the method `getGreeting` send a GET request to the controller of step 3. Leave the method body empty: Tachyon writes it.

In the service, `Needs` asks Tachyon to put a `GreetingClient` into the field `greetingClient`. The method `askServer` waits for the answer and saves its message in the field `message`. In TypeScript, the page has its own copy of the model in `client/models/Greeting.ts`, because the browser cannot read files in `server/`. Change the component, the service and add the client. The page file stays the same as in step 2.

Result: click Ask the server. The text Hello from Yon appears under the buttons. A path such as `/api/greeting` stays on the same origin, so no host needs to be listed. A request to another host needs that host in `tac.outgoing.hosts`.
